description: 00420's closure is several-hundred activations (1504 return defines / max 4 ascents). Determine whether that breadth is legitimate (35 Enum calls x List+Range x lambdas x reduce bridge) or bloated by over-specialization / shape-polymorphic accumulator (f98). If bloated, f98 shape-convergence may shrink the closure and ease the seal independent of the engine arc. Grounded findings only.

comments.text: SPIKE VERDICT: LEGITIMATE BREADTH, NOT over-specialization (hard numbers, release 685e63be5). 00420 final sealed root-0 closure = 281 distinct activations (337 ever seeded); seal re-walks it ~346x => O(closure^2). Top fns: reduce_while/3 Enum 25, List impl 20/20, reducer lambdas 12 each. The reduce_while activations fragment along 3 DISPATCH-RELEVANT dims: receiver ([int] vs Range struct), accumulator SHAPE ({[],int}/{[],:true}/{[],[]}/{[],[],int} - distinct physical layouts the reducer destructures), and reducer CAPTURE (the 4 take_while acts that look identical at reduce_while level carry 4 DISTINCT user predicates #67/#69/#70/#87 as captured input 0 - reduce_while-level display was capture-blind). No rendered (receiver,acc,reducer+capture) tuple maps to 2 activations => NO over-fragmenting key dimension; convergence_class/dispatch-mask already correct. SCALING IS LINEAR: activations ~= 14 + 9.2*calls (predicts exactly 337 at 35 calls); acts/call DECREASES 23->9.6 with scale (fixed runtime base + constant marginal) - over-spec would be super-linear. Bounded orthogonal note: ~250 transitional seed arrows (188 type-var, 62 any) co-exist with grounded finals during ascent (<=3 per capture) - normal seed->ground, not duplicate finals, shaves a constant not the slope. CONCLUSION: closure size is the real program size; no convergence fix shrinks it meaningfully; the path is the incremental seal (fz-f98.14.1), not collapsing activations. Over-specialization RULED OUT.

title: Spike: audit 00420 closure size — legitimate breadth vs over-specialization (does the take/drop/split family create more activations than necessary?)
